completar.title: Complete your retirement plan
completar.text: Without the year you want to stop and the income you want, we can’t calculate the effect of each choice.

reserva.title: Save {amount} in your emergency fund
reserva.text: The emergency fund comes first: it keeps you from using expensive credit when something unexpected happens.

divida.title: Pay {amount} more on your most expensive debt
divida.text: The interest on this debt costs more than your money earns. Once it’s paid off, the amount goes to your plan.

guardar.title: Save {amount} more per month
guardar.text: This amount goes into your retirement plan and starts earning dividends.

gasto.title: Cut {amount} from {category}
gasto.text: That’s 10% of your largest category last month. Saving the difference also shortens the path.

reserva.title: Emergency fund
reserva.description: Money set aside for the unexpected, like a loss of income or a repair, so you don’t have to go into debt.

have.emptyText: Add the account where you keep this money so it shows up here.

markEssential.title: Mark what’s essential
markEssential.text: You already have expenses logged, but none in an essential category. Mark housing, groceries, bills and anything else you can’t cut as essential.

logExpenses.title: Log this month’s expenses
logExpenses.text: To calculate your emergency fund, we need to know how much housing, groceries and bills cost. Log these expenses, or enter the total amount above.

complete.title: Your emergency fund is complete
complete.text: Keep this money set aside and top it up whenever you use it. What you save from now on can go to your goals.

completeExtra.title: Your emergency fund is complete
completeExtra.text: You have {amount} more than you need. This surplus can go to your goals. Keep the rest set aside and top it up whenever you use it.

createAccount.title: Create the emergency fund account
createAccount.text: Your emergency fund lives in one of your accounts. Create an account to keep this money and then select it here.

chooseAccount.title: Choose where your emergency fund is kept
chooseAccount.text: Select the account where you keep this money. If you don’t have a separate one yet, it’s worth creating one just for this.

setAmount.title: Decide how much to save per month
setAmount.text: Pick an amount that fits your month, even a small one. Then we can show when your emergency fund will be ready.

saveOne.title: Save {amount} this month
saveOne.text: Put this amount in {place}. Repeat every month until your emergency fund is complete.

saveMany.title: Save {amount} this month
saveMany.text: Put this amount in one of your emergency fund accounts. Repeat every month until your emergency fund is complete.

how.title: How it works
how.source: Where essential expenses come from. We add up everything you logged in categories marked as essential, including card purchases and debt installments. We use the average of the last 3 closed months. If you’re just getting started, you’ll see an estimate based on the current month, and you can enter the amount if you prefer.
how.mark: How to mark a category as essential. In Categories, edit the category and check “This is an essential expense”. From then on, expenses in that category count toward the calculation.
how.money: How money gets into the emergency fund. The emergency fund isn’t a new account: it adds up the balance of the accounts you select here. If the balance goes up or down, the fund follows.
